..
KEY MESSAGE 1)

Rain continues to blanket the area this afternoon, with rainfall
amounts generally 0.5-1.50 inches (central OH-northern KY) thus far,
with another 0.5-0.75 inches expected through tonight. The deepening
sfc low will continue to track to the N near the spine of the 
Appalachians while the midlevel low slowly trudges NE through the 
srn OH Vly and nrn TN Vly. 

Thermal profiles will remain too warm locally through midnight to 
support any mixing of rain with snow, but as the deeper-layer low 
centers pivot to our E during the predawn hours, the wind profile 
will become more westerly, supporting CAA within a deeper layer of 
the column. This will steepen lapse rates and usher in perhaps just 
enough cold air to support some mixing of snow with the rain early 
Friday morning. As we progress toward daybreak and beyond, drier air 
within the DGZ will become more pronounced, with the once very-deep 
moisture becoming increasingly shallow through the first part of the 
daytime. This, alongside less forcing, will yield an overall 
weakening/lightening of the banded precip into the afternoon. 
However, sporadic light banded precip may continue through the 
entire daytime before nudging to the E of the local area by sunset 
Friday evening. Cannot completely rule out a dusting of snow 
accumulation on grassy surfaces (mainly near/W of I-75 into ern IN) 
early morning if there are brief periods where the rain transitions 
completely to snow. But minimal impacts are expected given above 
freezing air temps and antecedent (very) warm ground conditions. Any 
very minor grassy/elevated accumulation will melt quickly into late 
morning and early afternoon.

The other item of interest through Friday is going to be the wind. A
relatively-tight sfc pressure gradient will support sustained NE 
winds of 15-20kts with occasional gusts to 25-30kts through this
afternoon. Although the BL is saturated and relatively shallow, the 
low-level and deep-layer flow fields are fairly robust. Into this 
afternoon, fcst soundings show a slight steepening of the LL lapse 
rates, suggesting a bit more mixing potential in the lowest 2kft,
particularly N of the OH Rvr. So despite the saturated nature of the
LL profile, some momentum transfer should bring some 30kt gusts 
mid/late afternoon during peak mixing, especially near/north of I-70.
Suppose a 35kt gust cannot be completely ruled out, particularly 
between 18z-22z.

As the elongated sfc low (with a trailing sfc trof) pivots N into the
ern OH Vly past 03z, winds should temporarily subside as the 
pressure gradient briefly relaxes through about 12z. However, after 
daybreak, the sfc pressure gradient should begin to tighten again. 
This, alongside increasing CAA through the column (steepening LL 
lapse rates), will support a gradual increase in sustained winds and 
gustiness into Friday afternoon continuing through the evening. 
Westerly winds of 15-20kts, with gusts to around 25-30kts, can be 
expected from about 20z-04z before gustiness tapers off to 20kts or 
less toward midnight and beyond.

KEY MESSAGE 2)
 
Brief midlevel ridging will build into the region Friday night into
early Saturday before flow becomes more zonal once again by Saturday
night. This will provide some tranquil weather across the OH Vly
before a digging trof and quick-moving system comes back in by early
Sunday. A strengthening system will translate into the mid MS/OH 
Vlys by early Sunday, promoting sfc cyclogenesis/deepening as the low
moves toward the ILN FA Sunday morning.

Widespread rain will overspread the area by late morning into the
afternoon as the dynamic system moves through the OH Vly. Despite a
deepening system and corresponding enhancement of the deep-layer and
LL wind fields, instby should remain very limited as sfc dewpoints
will struggle to reach into the lower 50s, even in N KY. As the sfc
low pulls east quickly Sunday evening into Sunday night, gusty winds
owing to a tightening pressure gradient/rapid height rises and
CAA/steepening lapse rates, will overspread the area. Gusts of 30-35
MPH are expected Sunday evening/night before relaxing into the
predawn hours as a sfc high builds in from the west for the daytime
Monday. 

Cooler air will filter in for Monday, but drier conditions and a 
warming trend are expected heading into the middle of next week.
